lab_title: Anatomy of the Human Heart: Structure and Circulatory Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the human heart.
Compare the structural differences between the right and left ventricles in relation to their workload.
Trace the pathway of blood flow through the pulmonary and systemic circulatory loops.
Explain the mechanical role of heart valves in maintaining unidirectional blood flow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the gross anatomy and external orientation of the heart.
key_visuals: A life-sized, anatomically correct 3D heart model floating in the student's space.
Labels indicating anterior, posterior, superior, and inferior aspects.
student_actions: Rotate and scale the heart model to identify major vessels: aorta, pulmonary trunk, and vena cava.
Use a virtual marker to highlight the path of the coronary arteries.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore the internal anatomy of the heart chambers.
key_visuals: The heart model transitions to a 'cut-away' view, revealing internal chambers.
Color-coded chambers (blue for deoxygenated side, red for oxygenated side).
student_actions: Tap each chamber to trigger a label and a short text summary of its function.
Compare the wall thickness (myocardium) of the right vs. left ventricles.

scenes.brief_purpose: Understand the structure and function of heart valves.
key_visuals: A magnified, isolated view of a valve.
Animation showing the valve opening and closing.
student_actions: Select each valve to observe its specific movement.
Simulate a 'backflow' scenario to observe how valves prevent regurgitation.

key_visuals: A pulsing light trail representing the path of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart to the lungs.
student_actions: Follow the light trail from the vena cava through the right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, and pulmonary artery.

key_visuals: A pulsing red light trail showing the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs, through the left side of the heart, to the aorta.
student_actions: Trace the path from the pulmonary veins, through the left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, and aortic valve into the aorta.

scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize knowledge by performing a full blood flow sequence.
key_visuals: A fully animated, synchronous heartbeat displaying continuous blood flow loops.
student_actions: Use the controller to speed up or slow down the heartbeat to observe how the structures interact in real-time.
Answer a series of interactive, pop-up knowledge check questions based on the full flow.
